findings.text: onTrimMemory drops every sparkline at TRIM_MEMORY_UI_HIDDEN (20 >= TRIM_RUNNING_CRITICAL 15), which Android delivers on EVERY app switch. The sparkAt 5-minute throttle is already stamped, so charts stay blank for up to 5 minutes after returning. This is TJ's 'charts disappeared when I switched back' report. The doc comment's reasoning ('they ride along with the next quote') went stale in Round 56 when the series moved off the quote path.
findings.note: onTrimMemory now releases nothing below TRIM_MODERATE (60); UI_HIDDEN no longer blanks charts

findings.text: After a spark drop the DB (quotes.spark) still holds the series, but nothing re-reads it on return - the recovery path is a network fetch that the throttle suppresses.
findings.note: restoreSparklines() reads quotes.spark back from SQLite on every resume; chart_cache does the same for fetched ranges

findings.text: refreshSparklines only unmarks sparkAt when EVERY symbol failed. On a partial failure the symbols that failed stay stamped 'just fetched' and are not retried for a full 5 minutes, so individual charts are intermittently missing - TJ's 'sometimes they don't load'.
findings.note: refreshSparklines un-marks every failed symbol, not only the all-failed case

findings.text: refreshSparklines is called at the very end of refresh(), AFTER the 'fetched.isEmpty() -> return@launch' early exit. One failed batch quote pass means the candle series is not refreshed at all that tick, even for symbols whose charts are blank.
findings.note: refreshSparklines starts alongside the quote pass, above the no-quotes early return

findings.text: MarketData.yahoo() and batchYahoo() return immediately when query1 is in a LOCAL cooldown instead of trying query2. Cooldowns are armed per host, so query1 cooling says nothing about query2 - the chart request is abandoned while a usable host sits unused. Contributes to charts not loading.
findings.note: a locally-cooling Yahoo host is now skipped rather than abandoning the request; both chart and batch paths

findings.text: fgScope cancellation on ON_STOP has no counterpart on ON_START for the DETAIL SCREEN's own loads. A stock opened and then backgrounded mid-fetch has its news/fundamentals/insider/chart/holdings request cancelled, and the LaunchedEffect(symbol) that started it does not re-fire on return because its key has not changed - so the tab stays empty until a manual pull-to-refresh. Introduced by Round 57's fgScope work; the chart and holdings added this round inherit it.
findings.note: DetailScreen re-requests its cache-first loads on ON_START, so an fgScope cancellation no longer strands an open screen

findings.text: The 1D chart request and the row-sparkline request are the SAME Yahoo URL (range=1d&interval=5m&includePrePost=true) fired on two independent 5-minute clocks. With a stock's detail screen open the app pulls that body twice per window for no benefit.
findings.note: loadChart(D1) feeds its series into the quote's spark and stamps sparkAt, so the identical sparkline request is not made

findings.text: ChartRange.OVERNIGHT silently degrades into a 5-day intraday chart when meta carries no tradingPeriods and no currentTradingPeriod: with no regular windows the extended-only filter keeps everything, and it is still captioned 'After-hours and overnight only'.

HoldingsTab keys its LazyColumn on symbol-or-name. Two share classes or a provider repeat give the same key, and a LazyColumn handed a duplicate key THROWS and takes the app down. This exact crash has shipped three times in this project (news, filings, research rows).

After a memory trim drops _holdings, a detail screen sitting on the HOLDINGS tab has that tab removed from the visible list while 'tab' still points at it: the indicator jumps to Overview while the Holdings body is still rendered.

adoptAsSparkline feeds the D1 chart series into quote.spark, but the two are NOT the same data: MarketData.parseYahoo puts only REGULAR-session points in spark, while ChartFeed keeps pre/post as well. The row sparkline would silently change from a trading-day line into a 24-hour one, with the prevClose baseline no longer matching what is drawn.
loadChart marks chartDiskRead BEFORE the disk read. A cancellation between the two leaves the symbol marked as read with nothing loaded, so the disk cache is never consulted again this session.
chart_cache uses a column literally named 'range', which is a reserved keyword in SQLite's window-frame syntax. Unquoted, it is at best relying on the parser's leniency.

purgeChartCache binds an Int via execSQL bind args. Android's SQLiteProgram binds only Long/Double/String/byte[]/null and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise - swallowed by runCatching, so the cache would grow unbounded and silently.
Opening a symbol from SearchSheet does not clear detailStack, so a back press from the searched stock returns to a fund left on the stack rather than dismissing the screen.

The new ON_START DisposableEffect is keyed on symbol/chartRange/tab, so it re-registers on every tab and range change - and LifecycleRegistry replays ON_START to a newly added observer, firing all six loads again each time.
